51555615.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to his tagged BRDT bromodomain (unknown origin) assessed as dissociation constant by SPR method

original_paragraph.SPR binding analysis of (+) JQ1-F analog: The Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) experiment was conducted using a Pioneer FE SPR System (Sartorius) equipped with a SPR HisCap Sensor Chip. The instrument was calibrated and validated prior to the experiment according to the manufacturer's instructions. The chip surface was activated with a mixture of N-hydroxysuccinimide (NHS), 50 mM, and N-ethyl-N'-(3-dimethylaminopropyl) carbodiimide (EDC), 200 mM, at a 20 μL/min flow rate for 5 minutes. Covalent attachment of his-BRDT to channel 1 was achieved by injecting 150 μL of protein at 10 mg/mL at 10 mL/min. Channel 2 of the chip was used as a blank reference and unreacted functional groups of both channels were blocked using ethanolamine. SPR running buffer consisted of 100 mM Tris-HCl, 200 mM NaCl, and 0.05% Tween-20. The JQ1 analog samples were prepared in a solution that closely mimics the buffer conditions and injected at 40 μL/min using the OneStep injection system at 0.5, 5, and 50 μM concentrations. The real-time binding response was recorded using the instrument software and sensorgrams were analyzed using the QDAT software. The baseline subtraction, referencing, and double-referencing techniques were applied to obtain specific binding responses. Kinetic parameters were calculated by fitting sensorgrams to OneStep binding models for determining the dissociation rate constant (k_d) for the highest concentration and constraining the lower concentrations to the determined value. All data was locally fitted to a simple 1:1 interaction model.
original_paragraph.Figure S13 caption: Figure S13. SPR binding data for (+)-JQ1-F analogs
original_paragraph.Figure S13 sensorgram: The sensorgram shows the response (RU) over time (s) for multiple analytes. The x-axis ranges from 0 to 300 seconds. The y-axis (Response) ranges from 0 to 80 RU. The curves show association (rising phase) and dissociation (falling phase) phases. The lower plot shows the residual (RU) over time, indicating the fit quality of the model to the data.
